record.paper_title: Five open problems in theory of quantum information
record.original_question: For Werner states ρ(d,α) on H_d⊗H_d, determine whether every Werner state that is not 1-copy distillable is nondistillable for all finite numbers of copies. Using the parameterization ρ(d,α) = (I⊗I + αV)/(d^2 + αd), where V is the swap operator, the conjecture says that 1-copy nondistillability should coincide with complete nondistillability for this family.

It was conjectured [133–136, 141] that the Werner states which are not 1-copy distillable are just not-distillable, so in particular they are also2-copy non-distillable.
A stronger conjecture that for Werner states 1-copy nondistillability is equivalent to complete non-distillability, means that B∞= B1 in Fig. 5.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H_d$ denote a $d$-dimensional complex Hilbert space, and let $V$ be the swap (flip) operator on $H_d \otimes H_d$ defined by $\langle ij | V | kl \rangle = \delta_{il}\delta_{jk}$. For $d \geq 2$ and $\alpha \in [-1, 1]$, define the Werner state
$$\rho(d,\alpha) = \frac{I \otimes I + \alpha V}{d^2 + \alpha d}.$$
A bipartite state $\rho$ acting on $H_A \otimes H_B$ is called $n$-copy distillable if there exist a Schmidt-rank-2 vector $|\psi\rangle \in (H_A^{\otimes n}) \otimes (H_B^{\otimes n})$ and local operators $A, B$ acting on $H_A^{\otimes n}, H_B^{\otimes n}$ respectively such that
$$\langle \psi | (A \otimes B)\, \rho^{\otimes n} (A \otimes B)^\dagger | \psi \rangle > \tfrac{1}{2} \langle \psi | (A \otimes B)(A \otimes B)^\dagger | \psi \rangle \cdot \mathrm{Tr}(\rho^{\otimes n}(A\otimes B)^\dagger(A\otimes B))/\mathrm{Tr}((A\otimes B)^\dagger(A\otimes B)\rho^{\otimes n}),$$
equivalently, such that $(A \otimes B)\,\rho^{\otimes n}(A \otimes B)^\dagger$, suitably normalized, has fidelity greater than $1/2$ with a maximally entangled two-qubit state under the projection onto the support of $|\psi\rangle$. The state $\rho$ is called distillable if it is $n$-copy distillable for some finite $n$, and completely non-distillable otherwise.

Prove or disprove: for every dimension $d \geq 2$ and every parameter $\alpha \in [-1,1]$ such that the Werner state $\rho(d,\alpha)$ is not $1$-copy distillable, $\rho(d,\alpha)$ is not $n$-copy distillable for any finite $n \geq 1$ (in particular, $1$-copy non-distillability is equivalent to complete non-distillability within the Werner family).
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture, equivalent to the existence of NPT bound entangled Werner states, has been studied since the late 1990s and remains open as of 2024. Recent work (e.g., arXiv:2402.18037) continues to investigate the distillability sets of Werner states and the associated 2-copy "half-property" without resolving the full conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Unveiling NPT bound problem: From Distillability Sets to Inequalities and Multivariable Insights
status_evidence.snippet: The problem of whether 1-copy undistillable Werner states are completely undistillable is studied; reduces to the half-property for two copies.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture remains an active open problem as of 2024.

status_evidence.title: A few steps more towards NPT bound entanglement
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates n-copy distillability of Werner states; reduces problem to maximum overlap of certain projectors with Schmidt rank 2 vectors.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier partial progress, problem still open.
